papers.title: A Constructive Approach to $q$-Gaussian Distributions: $α$-Divergence as Rate Function and Generalized de Moivre-Laplace Theorem
papers.summary: The paper presents a constructive approach to derive power-law distributions, specifically the q-Gaussian distribution, using a nonlinear differential equation and finite counting.
papers.main_problem: The main problem addressed by the paper is to establish a constructive probabilistic framework for power-law distributions, comparable to the classical binomial process.
papers.main_contribution: The main contribution of the paper is a generalized binomial distribution based on finite counting, which leads to a q-Gaussian distribution, and the identification of the α-divergence as the rate function.
papers.applications: Potential applications include understanding and modeling power-law distributions in various fields, such as physics, finance, and social sciences.
papers.limitations: The paper focuses on the regime 0 < q < 1 and the breakdown of the macroscopic scaling for heavier tails (q > 1), which may limit its applicability to other regimes.

papers.summary: The paper explores the probabilistic interpretation of the Selberg--Delange Method in analytic number theory, showing mod-Poisson convergence for the number of distinct prime factors of a randomly chosen integer.
